content.name: Alabama
content.tip: Montgomery sits in the middle of Alabama — think of a gum tree in the center.

content.name: Alaska
content.tip: Juneau is so far southeast you cannot drive there from the rest of Alaska.

content.name: Arizona
content.tip: A phoenix rises from desert heat — Arizona's capital is the hottest big city.

content.name: Arkansas
content.tip: Picture a little rock sitting on the Arkansas River.

content.name: California
content.tip: Not LA or San Francisco — the capital is inland, Sacramento.

content.name: Colorado
content.tip: The Mile High City — Denver is a mile above sea level.

content.name: Connecticut
content.tip: A hart is an old word for a deer — Hartford, heart of Connecticut.

content.name: Delaware
content.tip: Dover like the white cliffs — Delaware's capital is a small town, not Wilmington.

content.name: Florida
content.tip: Far north in the panhandle, not Miami. Tallahassee: 'tell a hassy'.

content.name: Georgia
content.tip: Atlanta is the big hub — planes, peaches, and the capital.

content.name: Hawaii
content.tip: Honolulu is on Oahu — the only island most visitors land on first.

content.name: Idaho
content.tip: Boise sounds like 'boy-see' — potatoes and a boy you see.

content.name: Illinois
content.tip: Lincoln's town, not Chicago. Springfield is in the middle of the state.

content.name: Indiana
content.tip: The capital's name starts with the state: Indiana-polis.

content.name: Iowa
content.tip: Say 'duh moyn' — French name, Iowa heartland.

content.name: Kansas
content.tip: Topeka: 'toe-peek-uh' — peek at the prairie.

content.name: Kentucky
content.tip: Not Louisville. Frankfort is a small river town with a frank name.

content.name: Louisiana
content.tip: French for 'red stick' — not New Orleans.

content.name: Maine
content.tip: Augusta, not Portland. Think August on the Kennebec River.

content.name: Maryland
content.tip: Navy town on the bay — Annapolis, not Baltimore.

content.name: Massachusetts
content.tip: Boston is both the biggest city and the capital.

content.name: Michigan
content.tip: Not Detroit. Lansing sits between the two peninsulas' mainland.

content.name: Minnesota
content.tip: Twin Cities: Minneapolis is bigger; Saint Paul is the capital.

content.name: Mississippi
content.tip: Jackson, like Andrew Jackson, right in the middle of the state.

content.name: Missouri
content.tip: Named for Jefferson — not St. Louis or Kansas City.

content.name: Montana
content.tip: Helena: 'hell-uh-nuh' — a small mountain capital, not Billings.

content.name: Nebraska
content.tip: Lincoln, not Omaha. Another capital named for the president.

content.name: Nevada
content.tip: Tiny Carson City, not Las Vegas or Reno.

content.name: New Hampshire
content.tip: Concord like the grape — not Manchester.

content.name: New Jersey
content.tip: Washington crossed the Delaware to Trenton. Not Newark.

content.name: New Mexico
content.tip: Santa Fe is older than the United States — not Albuquerque.

content.name: New York
content.tip: Up the Hudson, not New York City. Albany is the capital.

content.name: North Carolina
content.tip: Raleigh: 'rah-lee' — Research Triangle, not Charlotte.

content.name: North Dakota
content.tip: Bismarck, named for a German chancellor — not Fargo.

content.name: Ohio
content.tip: Columbus is in the center of Ohio, like a compass rose.

content.name: Oklahoma
content.tip: The capital and the biggest city share the state's name.

content.name: Oregon
content.tip: Salem, not Portland. Same name as a famous Massachusetts town.

content.name: Pennsylvania
content.tip: Harrisburg on the Susquehanna — not Philadelphia or Pittsburgh.

content.name: Rhode Island
content.tip: Providence: the smallest state's capital is right on the bay.

content.name: South Carolina
content.tip: Columbia in the middle — not Charleston on the coast.

content.name: South Dakota
content.tip: Say 'peer', not 'pee-air'. Tiny Pierre, not Sioux Falls.

content.name: Tennessee
content.tip: Music City is also the capital.

content.name: Texas
content.tip: Keep Austin weird — not Houston or Dallas.

content.name: Utah
content.tip: Named for the Great Salt Lake just beside it.

content.name: Vermont
content.tip: Smallest capital city in the U.S. — not Burlington.

content.name: Virginia
content.tip: Richmond on the James River — not Virginia Beach or Norfolk.

content.name: Washington
content.tip: Olympia, near the Olympic Mountains — not Seattle.

content.name: West Virginia
content.tip: Charleston, West Virginia — not the one in South Carolina.

content.name: Wisconsin
content.tip: Madison sits on an isthmus between two lakes — not Milwaukee.

content.name: Wyoming
content.tip: Cheyenne: 'shy-ann' — a frontier name on the plains.
